synopsis: The booklet recommends reference class forecasting plus schedule-risk analysis as the primary schedule approach for collision-mitigation validation, using P50/P80 to establish time credibility [f10070, f9592]. The glossary places this approach within a layered planning architecture, alongside verification and validation planning, evidence-based gates, uncertainty methods, and a communication roadmap [f16428]. Its fit is rated high for high uncertainty and a fixed deadline when the reference class is similar; comparative findings and planning-fallacy experiments provide supporting evidence [f10064, f10065, f10066]. However, reference-class selection is difficult and the underlying mechanism is contested, yielding an overall verdict of supported but contested [f10068, f10067, f10069]. The approach is associated with Flyvbjerg 2006 and GAO-16-89G [f10062].
